title: Đưa 5 vị trí wire về một hằng số WIRE_NAME
one_line: Add one named constant, WIRE_NAME, whose value is deliberately still the string "omp", and point the five third-party contract sites at it so the next rename has one place to change instead of five — and, because four of the five already have golden-literal tests, so that renaming it breaks a test instead of a user's Warp terminal or ACP client.
user_visible_effect: none — internal. This commit must be byte-for-byte invisible: the constant's value is "omp", identical to every literal it replaces. The visible effect is deferred to W7/W9, where a reviewer can see a rename touch one constant rather than argue about which of five occurrences was the wire value. The single user-visible risk is the one this item exists to prevent: if WIRE_NAME is ever set to the NEW name in this commit, Warp's OSC agent prefix, the ACP agentInfo.title, the DAP initialize clientID/clientName, the puush multipart `z` field, and the default Hindsight bank id all change together and break silently — no error, just a Warp terminal that stops attributing events, a DAP adapter that stops matching the client, and a memory bank that splits in two. Four existing golden tests catch that; this item's new test is what makes the constant itself, not just the sites, a pinned contract.

test_contract: The observable contract: a third party reading our DAP initialize request, our Warp OSC-777 event, our ACP agentInfo, our puush multipart upload, or our default Hindsight bank id sees the exact bytes they saw before this commit, and a future rename of the shared identity constant fails a test instead of silently splitting our identity across those five integrations. Concretely, four of the five sites ALREADY have golden-literal tests that go red if the value changes — warp-events.test.ts:111 pins `agent: "omp"` inside an exact JSON.stringify of the whole OSC body; acp-initialize-conformance.test.ts:237 pins `title: "omp"` via objectContaining; blob-uploaders-self-hosted-legacy.test.ts:342 pins `form.get("z") === "omp"`; hindsight-bank.test.ts pins the derived ids `"omp"`, `"omp-proj"`, `"omp-unknown"`, `"omp-general"`. Those four must be LEFT ALONE — they are the golden pins, and converting them to compare against `WIRE_NAME` would destroy the only mechanism that catches a bad rename. The one new test defends what the four cannot: that the SHARED CONSTANT ITSELF still holds that byte string. It lives in packages/utils/test/wire-name.test.ts because that suite runs without the native addon (verified: `bun test packages/utils/test/dirs.test.ts` → 6 pass 0 fail), whereas every coding-agent test file is currently unrunnable (verified: warp-events.test.ts → 0 pass 1 fail, missing pi_natives.darwin-arm64.node). KNOWN GAP, stated rather than papered over: the DAP site (dap/session.ts:1465-1466) has NO test of its own — `#buildInitializeArguments` is an ES #private method reached only through the full DapSessionManager launch path, and the repo has no DAP test file (only `packages/coding-agent/test/dap-write-sink-flush.typecheck.ts`). It is covered TRANSITIVELY: all five sites read one constant, so the four goldens plus the new constant test pin the value the DAP site emits. If a reviewer wants a direct DAP assertion, the seam is `vi.spyOn(DapClient, "spawn")` returning a stub whose `initialize` records its first argument — but that drags the whole launch path into a 2-line change and is not recommended for this item. Consumer-visible regression if the contract breaks: a Warp terminal stops attributing events to omp, an ACP client shows the wrong agent title, a DAP debug adapter stops recognising our initialize request, a puush upload is rejected or filed under an unknown author, and existing Hindsight memories land in a bank the user can no longer reach — all without a single thrown error.

gate:
The change is DONE when all of the following hold, and the first one is the one that can fail:

(1) `bun test packages/utils/test/wire-name.test.ts` FAILS if `WIRE_NAME` is not exactly the string "omp" — verified by temporarily setting it to "ultraworkers" and confirming a red run, then reverting. This is the load-bearing gate: it is the only thing that pins the constant itself, and it is the whole defence against the failure mode the plan calls out first.
(2) `bun run check:ts` is green.
(3) All four existing golden test files are byte-identical to HEAD — `git diff packages/coding-agent/test/ packages/catalog/` is EMPTY. If any of them changed, the engineer converted a golden pin into a tautology and the item is not done, regardless of whether tests pass.
(4) `git diff --stat` lists exactly the six modified source files plus the one new test file, and `packages/catalog/src/wire/codex.ts` is not among them.
(5) `git grep -n '"omp"'` over the four coding-agent source files that had bare literals returns zero hits, while `acp-agent.ts` retains `name: "oh-my-pi"` on line 656.
(6) `packages/coding-agent/src/dap/session.ts` shows no new test file and no new export — the DAP gap was closed transitively, as documented, rather than by adding a harness.
gate_can_fail: Yes, and gate (1) is the one that bites. It goes red the moment someone writes `export const WIRE_NAME: string = "ultraworkers";` — which is the single most likely mistake here, because the whole point of the constant is to be renamed and the new brand name is the most attractive thing in the repo to type. The four existing goldens are a second, independent net for the same mistake (they compare against literal "omp"), and gate (3) catches the subtler failure where an engineer "helpfully" rewrites those goldens to compare against the constant, which would make all five sites pass a rename silently. Gate (4) catches scope creep — the plan itself warns that adding a sixth site is the second-most-likely error, and `git grep` over the whole repo finds several more bare "omp" wire values (see plan_corrections) that an eager engineer would fold in without deciding. Nothing in this gate is a tautology or a bare not.toThrow(); every clause names a value a third party reads.
effort: S for the source change (six files, one added line in dirs.ts and five one-to-three-line edits), S for the test (one new ~15-line file, zero edits to existing tests). Net roughly 40 lines of diff across 7 paths. The plan's "~10 lines" understates it by not counting the new test file, but the plan's instinct that this is the cheapest item in the wave is right. The one thing that could blow it up is the DAP test — gate (6) exists specifically to stop that from happening.
risk: Typing the new brand name into WIRE_NAME. This is the failure the plan names first and it is genuinely the most likely one, because the constant exists to be renamed and the new name is sitting right there in the milestone description. If it happens, all five integrations change identity simultaneously and NOTHING throws: a Warp terminal stops attributing events, an ACP client shows the wrong title, a DAP adapter stops matching the client, a puush upload is filed under an unknown author, and every Hindsight memory the user has lands in a bank they can no longer reach. The second-order variant is the mirror image and just as bad: an engineer sees the four golden tests fail and "fixes" them by comparing against `WIRE_NAME` instead of the literal — which makes the rename invisible to the test suite forever after, and defeats the entire purpose of the item. Gate (3) exists for that case specifically. Do not let W3's APP_NAME change leak in here either: WIRE_NAME must be its own literal, not an alias of APP_NAME, or changing the display name in W3 would silently move the wire value.
open_questions: The plan says the wire set is five positions, but `git grep -n '"omp"' -- packages/{coding-agent,catalog,utils,tui}/src` finds several more bare-literal wire values this item does not touch. Two of them are serious and are NOT display strings: `packages/catalog/src/compat/rules/auth/stencil.kdl:13` (`client-id "omp"` — the OAuth client id registered at the Stencil issuer; renaming it breaks Stencil login, and per AGENTS.md it lives in KDL so a TS constant cannot simply be substituted) and `packages/catalog/src/compat/rules/auth/openai-codex.kdl:12` (`originator "omp"`). Non-KDL extras: `packages/coding-agent/src/cli/git-tui/avatar.ts:50` (`"User-Agent": "omp"` on the GitHub API), `packages/coding-agent/src/tools/report-tool-issue.ts:441` (`agent: { name: "omp" }` in a POSTed grievance body), `packages/coding-agent/src/internal-urls/omp-protocol.ts:28` (`readonly scheme = "omp"` — the omp:// URL scheme). HUMAN DECISION: does the milestone owner want these folded into W1's wire set, assigned to a later work item, or explicitly recorded as do-not-touch? Do NOT silently add them — the plan explicitly forbids a sixth site — and do NOT silently leave them either, or W7's `sed` and W8b's display-token sweep become the thing that decides. My recommendation is a separate, explicit work item, because the two KDL ones need a KDL-level fix that this item must not attempt.

`packages/catalog/src/wire/codex.ts:52` is declared READ-ONLY by this item, but its real source is the writable KDL rule `packages/catalog/src/compat/rules/auth/openai-codex.kdl:12`. The compiled `rules.json` is committed. So a later `sed`-style pass over the KDL tree, or a `bun run gen:compat` after an unrelated KDL edit, can move this value with no TypeScript diff at all. HUMAN DECISION: who owns the invariant that the OpenAI originator stays "omp", and does it need a test before W7 runs? This is a real hole in the plan's own framing, not a hypothetical.

The DAP site (`dap/session.ts:1465-1466`) has no direct test and I recommend not building a harness for it. HUMAN DECISION: accept transitive coverage (all five sites read one constant, and four goldens plus the new constant test pin its value), or spend the effort on a `vi.spyOn(DapClient, "spawn")` harness? The DAP `clientID`/`clientName` pair is the only one of the five whose consumer is a third-party debug adapter rather than an in-repo subsystem, so it is the one where a silent break is least likely to be noticed by the maintainers themselves.

`packages/coding-agent/src/hindsight/settings.ts:172` registers `cfgHindsightRetainContext` with `default: "omp"` — the same bank-namespace identity as `bank.ts:29`, but a separate persisted config key with its own default. Five test files carry `retainContext: "omp"` as a FIXTURE INPUT (hindsight-bank.test.ts:55, hindsight-conversation-timestamps.test.ts:35, hindsight-mm-cache-stability.test.ts:34, hindsight-retention-cache.test.ts:27, memory-tools.test.ts:63). HUMAN DECISION: is this the same wire identity (in which case it should also read WIRE_NAME, changing an existing default and its persisted value) or an independent user-facing setting default (in which case it stays)? I have left it out of W1 because changing a registered setting's default is a behaviour change, not a refactor, and that is W3's territory. Flagging it because five test fixtures currently hardcode it and the next person to sweep literals will trip on it.

plan_corrections.claim: `packages/catalog/src/wire/codex.ts:52` is a read-only reference point, and the wire set is exactly the five sites plus this file.
plan_corrections.verdict: PARTLY WRONG — the file is genuinely read-only, but its upstream source is not, and the plan's framing hides a live hazard.
plan_corrections.correction: The anchor is real (`ORIGINATOR_CODEX: "omp"` at line 52, confirmed, and it feeds `OPENAI_HEADERS.ORIGINATOR` at 8 call sites across packages/ai, packages/agent, packages/catalog, packages/coding-agent). But it is not a hand-written literal — it compiles from `packages/catalog/src/compat/rules/auth/openai-codex.kdl:12` (`originator "omp"`). AGENTS.md forbids hand-editing the compiled `rules.json`, so the only way to change this value is to edit the KDL. Consequence: W7's `git grep -o '@oh-my-pi/'` sweep does not touch it (no slash), W8b's display-token sweep might, and a `bun run gen:compat` after an unrelated KDL edit can move the originator with no TypeScript diff. plan_corrections.correction: If a test asserts `emitted === WIRE_NAME`, then setting `WIRE_NAME = "ultraworkers"` makes every such test pass while breaking all five integrations. The constant is the thing being renamed; the literal is the contract. The golden-literal assertions already in the tree are the correct design and must be preserved verbatim: `warp-events.test.ts:111` pins `agent: "omp"` inside an exact `JSON.stringify` of the whole OSC body, `acp-initialize-conformance.test.ts:237` pins `title: "omp"`, `blob-uploaders-self-hosted-legacy.test.ts:342` pins `form.get("z") === "omp"`, and `hindsight-bank.test.ts` pins the derived ids `"omp"`/`"omp-proj"`/`"omp-unknown"`/`"omp-general"`. The correct split is two-sided and the plan collapsed it: the EXISTING tests keep the literal (they defend the wire bytes), and the ONE new test pins that the shared constant still equals that literal (it defends that the sites read the constant at all). If the new test also compared against the constant, the rename detection would evaporate.
